subject: Chemistry
sectionTitle: Balancing Equations, Combination, Decomposition, Displacement, Double Displacement & Redox
content:
Chemical Reactions & Balancing:
A process in which reactants transform into products with new physical and chemical properties. According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, the number of atoms of each element must remain equal on both sides of a balanced chemical equation.
Types of Chemical Reactions:
1. Combination Reaction: Two or more substances combine to form a single product:
   CaO(s) + H₂O(l) --> Ca(OH)₂(aq) + Heat  (Quicklime to Slaked lime, highly exothermic).
2. Decomposition Reaction: A single reactant breaks down into simpler products:
   - Thermal: 2FeSO₄(s) --Heat--> Fe₂O₃(s) + SO₂(g) + SO₃(g); CaCO₃ --Heat--> CaO + CO₂
   - Electrolytic: 2H₂O(l) --Electricity--> 2H₂(g) + O₂(g)
   - Photolytic: 2AgCl(s) --Sunlight--> 2Ag(s) + Cl₂(g) (used in black-and-white photography).
3. Displacement Reaction: A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution:
   Fe(s) + CuSO₄(aq) [Blue] --> FeSO₄(aq) [Green] + Cu(s) [Brown deposit].
4. Double Displacement Reaction: Mutual exchange of ions between two compounds forming an insoluble precipitate:
   Na₂SO₄(aq) + BaCl₂(aq) --> BaSO₄(s) [White ppt] + 2NaCl(aq).
5. Oxidation and Reduction (Redox):
   - Oxidation: Gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen/electrons.
   - Reduction: Loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen/electrons.
   CuO + H₂ --Heat--> Cu + H₂O (CuO is reduced to Cu; H₂ is oxidised to H₂O).
Effects in Everyday Life:
- Corrosion: Slow oxidation of metals by air, moisture, and acids (Rusting of iron: hydrated ferric oxide Fe₂O₃·xH₂O; green coating on copper: basic copper carbonate; black silver sulphide on silver).
- Rancidity: Oxidation of fats and oils in food causing foul smell and rancid taste, prevented by adding antioxidants and flushing packets with unreactive Nitrogen gas.
formulas: CaO + H₂O --> Ca(OH)₂ + Heat  (Quicklime to Slaked Lime)
2AgCl --Sunlight--> 2Ag + Cl₂  (Photolytic Decomposition)
Fe + CuSO₄ --> FeSO₄ + Cu  (Displacement)
Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ --> BaSO₄(s) + 2NaCl  (Double Displacement Precipitation)

ncertQuestions.question: Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction?
ncertQuestions.answer: During digestion, food carbohydrates are broken down into glucose. In cellular respiration, glucose combines with oxygen in cells releasing energy in the form of ATP: C6H12O6 + 6O2 -> 6CO2 + 6H2O + Energy (ATP).

summary: Chemical equations are balanced to conserve mass. Reactions include Combination, Decomposition, Displacement, Double Displacement (precipitation), and Redox. Corrosion and rancidity result from oxidation.

subject: Chemistry
sectionTitle: pH Scale, Importance in Everyday Life, Bleaching Powder, Baking Soda, Washing Soda & Plaster of Paris
content:
Acids and Bases in Aqueous Solution:
- Acids produce H₃O⁺ (hydronium) ions in water: HCl + H₂O --> H₃O⁺ + Cl⁻.
- Bases produce OH⁻ (hydroxide) ions in water: NaOH --> Na⁺ + OH⁻. Water-soluble bases are called Alkalis.
The pH Scale:
Measures hydrogen ion concentration: pH = -log₁₀[H⁺].
- Neutral: pH = 7. Acidic: pH < 7. Basic / Alkaline: pH > 7.
Everyday pH Significance:
- Human body operates within narrow pH range of 7.0 to 7.8.
- Acid Rain: Rainwater with pH < 5.6, harming aquatic life.
- Tooth Decay: Enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite) corrodes when mouth pH falls below 5.5 due to acid-producing bacteria.
Common Commercial Salts:
1. Bleaching Powder (CaOCl₂): Produced by reaction of chlorine gas on dry slaked lime:
   Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ --> CaOCl₂ + H₂O (disinfectant and bleaching agent in textile/paper industry).
2. Baking Soda (Sodium hydrogen carbonate, NaHCO₃):
   NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ --> NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃.
   On heating: 2NaHCO₃ --Heat--> Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ (CO₂ bubbles make cakes soft and spongy).
3. Washing Soda (Na₂CO₃·10H₂O): Sodium carbonate decahydrate, used in glass/soap industry and removing permanent water hardness.
4. Plaster of Paris (CaSO₄·½H₂O): Calcium sulphate hemihydrate, made by heating gypsum at 373 K:
   CaSO₄·2H₂O --373K--> CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½ H₂O. Rehydrates back into hard solid gypsum.
formulas: pH = -log₁₀[H⁺]  (Scale: 0 - 14, Neutral = 7)
Ca(OH)₂ + Cl₂ --> CaOCl₂ + H₂O  (Bleaching Powder)
2NaHCO₃ --Heat--> Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂  (Baking Soda)
CaSO₄·2H₂O --373 K--> CaSO₄·½H₂O + 1½ H₂O  (Plaster of Paris)

ncertQuestions.question: What is the commercial name and formula of Plaster of Paris? Why should it be stored in moisture-proof containers?
ncertQuestions.answer: Plaster of Paris is Calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO4·1/2H2O). It must be kept in moisture-proof containers because it absorbs atmospheric water to form hard rock gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O), losing its setting property.

summary: pH scale (0-14) indicates acidity (<7 acid, 7 neutral, >7 base). Essential salts: Bleaching powder CaOCl₂, Baking soda NaHCO₃, Washing soda Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, and Plaster of Paris CaSO₄·½H₂O.

subject: Chemistry
sectionTitle: Reactivity Series, Ionic Bonds, Metallurgy (Roasting, Calcination), Thermite Reaction & Alloys
content:
Reactivity Series of Metals (Decreasing order):
K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > [H] > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au.
Ionic Bonding:
Metals lose valence electrons forming cations; non-metals gain electrons forming anions. Electrostatic attraction binds them into Ionic Compounds (e.g., Na⁺ + Cl⁻ --> NaCl; Mg²⁺ + 2Cl⁻ --> MgCl₂).
Properties of Ionic Compounds: High melting/boiling points due to strong inter-ionic electrostatic bonds, solid and brittle, soluble in water, conduct electricity in molten state or aqueous solution.
Metallurgy (Extraction of Metals from Ores):
- Ores vs Minerals: Minerals from which metals can be extracted profitably are Ores.
- Concentration of Ore / Gangue removal.
- Moderate Reactivity Metals (Zinc, Iron):
  1. Roasting: Heating sulphide ores strongly in presence of excess air: 2ZnS + 3O₂ --Heat--> 2ZnO + 2SO₂.
  2. Calcination: Heating carbonate ores strongly in limited air: ZnCO₃ --Heat--> ZnO + CO₂.
  3. Reduction with Carbon: ZnO + C --> Zn + CO.
- High Reactivity Metals (Aluminium, Sodium): Extracted by Electrolytic Reduction of molten chloride/oxide (Aluminium extracted from molten Al₂O₃ using cryolite).
- Thermite Reaction: Reduction of iron oxide by aluminium powder:
  Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) --> 2Fe(l) + Al₂O₃(s) + Heat (molten iron joins railway tracks).
- Alloys: Homogeneous mixture of two or more metals, or a metal and a non-metal:
  Brass (Cu + Zn), Bronze (Cu + Sn), Solder (Pb + Sn, low melting point), Stainless Steel (Fe + Ni + Cr + C). Amalgam is an alloy containing Mercury.
formulas: Roasting: 2ZnS + 3O₂ --Heat--> 2ZnO + 2SO₂
Calcination: ZnCO₃ --Heat--> ZnO + CO₂
Thermite: Fe₂O₃ + 2Al --> 2Fe(l) + Al₂O₃ + Heat
Alloys: Brass (Cu+Zn), Bronze (Cu+Sn), Solder (Pb+Sn), Stainless Steel (Fe+Ni+Cr+C)

ncertQuestions.question: What is the thermite reaction? Mention its industrial application.
ncertQuestions.answer: The thermite reaction is the highly exothermic reduction of iron(III) oxide by aluminium powder: Fe2O3(s) + 2Al(s) -> 2Fe(l) + Al2O3(s) + Heat. The immense heat melts iron, which is used on-site to weld cracked railway tracks and heavy machine parts.

summary: Reactivity series dictates extraction: electrolytic reduction for reactive metals (Na, Al), roasting/calcination with carbon for moderate metals (Zn, Fe). Thermite reaction yields molten iron for rails. Alloys improve metal properties.

subject: Chemistry
sectionTitle: Covalent Bonding, Catenation, Tetravalency, Homologous Series, Esterification & Micelle Cleansing
content:
Covalent Bonding in Carbon:
Carbon (atomic number 6, electronic configuration 2,4) cannot form C⁴⁺ (requires enormous energy to remove 4 electrons) or C⁴⁻ (6 protons cannot hold 10 electrons). Hence, carbon shares its 4 valence electrons forming 4 Covalent Bonds.
Versatile Nature of Carbon:
1. Catenation: Unique property of carbon atoms to link with one another forming long chains, branched chains, or closed rings.
2. Tetravalency: Capability of bonding with 4 other monovalent atoms.
Hydrocarbons:
- Saturated (Alkanes, single bonds C-C): General formula C_n H_(2n+2) (e.g., CH₄, C₂H₆).
- Unsaturated:
  * Alkenes (double bond C=C): General formula C_n H_(2n) (e.g., C₂H₄ Ethene).
  * Alkynes (triple bond C≡C): General formula C_n H_(2n-2) (e.g., C₂H₂ Ethyne).
Homologous Series:
Family of organic compounds with same functional group where adjacent members differ by a -CH₂- unit and 14 u molecular mass.
Key Organic Chemical Reactions:
- Combustion: CH₄ + 2O₂ --> CO₂ + 2H₂O + Heat and Light.
- Addition Reaction (Hydrogenation): Unsaturated vegetable oils + H₂ --Ni catalyst--> Saturated vegetable ghee.
- Esterification: Ethanoic acid + Ethanol --conc. H₂SO₄--> Ethyl ethanoate (fruity sweet smell ester) + Water.
- Saponification: Alkaline hydrolysis of esters producing soap:
  CH₃COOC₂H₅ + NaOH --> CH₃COONa (Soap) + C₂H₅OH.
Soaps and Detergents (Micelle Mechanism):
- Soap molecule has a hydrophilic ionic head (-COO⁻Na⁺) and a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail.
- In water, tails orient inward toward oily dirt, while heads face outwards, forming a spherical cluster called a Micelle which emulsifies grease and washes it away.
formulas: Alkanes: C_n H_(2n+2)
Alkenes: C_n H_(2n)
Alkynes: C_n H_(2n-2)
Esterification: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH --H⁺--> CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O
Hydrogenation: R₂C=CR₂ + H₂ --Ni--> R₂CH-CHR₂

ncertQuestions.question: Explain the formation of micelles and the cleansing action of soap.
ncertQuestions.answer: Soap molecules have a hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail and a hydrophilic ionic head. In water, hydrophobic tails attach to oily dirt while hydrophilic heads face outward towards water, creating a spherical micelle that suspends dirt in water for easy rinsing.

summary: Carbon forms covalent bonds via catenation and tetravalency. Alkanes CnH2n+2, Alkenes CnH2n, Alkynes CnH2n-2. Esters give fruity fragrance; soaps cleanse by forming spherical micelles.

subject: Chemistry
sectionTitle: Dobereiner's Triads, Newlands' Octaves, Mendeleev's Periodic Law & Modern Periodic Table (Moseley)
content:
Historical Milestones in Element Classification:
1. Döbereiner's Triads (1817): Grouped elements in triads where atomic mass of middle element was roughly the arithmetic mean of the other two (e.g., Li 6.9, Na 23, K 39; Ca 40, Sr 87.6, Ba 137).
2. Newlands' Law of Octaves (1866): Arranged elements by increasing atomic masses; every eighth element had properties similar to the first (like musical notes Sa, Re, Ga...). Failed after Calcium; did not accommodate noble gases.
3. Mendeleev's Periodic Table (1869):
   - Periodic Law: 'The properties of elements are the periodic function of their atomic masses.'
   - Predicted undiscovered elements and left gaps (Eka-boron -> Scandium, Eka-aluminium -> Gallium, Eka-silicon -> Germanium).
   - Limitations: Position of Hydrogen anomalous; isotopes could not be assigned separate positions; anomalous atomic mass order (Co before Ni).
Modern Periodic Table (Henry Moseley, 1913):
- Modern Periodic Law: 'Properties of elements are a periodic function of their Atomic Number (Z).'
- Structure: 18 vertical columns called Groups and 7 horizontal rows called Periods.
Periodic Trends in Properties:
- Valency: Across period, increases from 1 to 4 then decreases to 0; remains constant down a group.
- Atomic Size (Radius): Decreases across a period (due to increasing nuclear charge pulling electrons inward); increases down a group (due to addition of new electron shells).
- Metallic Character: Decreases across a period (electropositive to electronegative); increases down a group.
- Non-metallic Character: Increases across a period; decreases down a group.
formulas: Mendeleev Law: Properties = f(Atomic Mass)
Modern Periodic Law: Properties = f(Atomic Number Z)
Trends: Atomic Size decreases across Period, increases down Group

ncertQuestions.question: How does the electronic configuration of an atom relate to its position in the Modern Periodic Table?
ncertQuestions.answer: The number of valence electrons determines the group number (e.g., 2 valence electrons = Group 2), and the total number of electron shells determines the period number (e.g., 3 shells K, L, M = Period 3).

summary: Mendeleev arranged elements by atomic mass; Moseley's Modern Periodic Table arranges 18 groups and 7 periods by atomic number Z. Atomic radius decreases across periods and increases down groups.

subject: Biology
sectionTitle: Nutrition, Aerobic/Anaerobic Respiration, Double Circulation & Excretion (Nephron)
content:
Life processes are the essential physiological maintenance functions:
1. Nutrition:
   - Autotrophic: Photosynthesis 6CO₂ + 6H₂O --> C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
   - Heterotrophic (Humans): Mouth (salivary amylase digests starch) -> Stomach (HCl activates pepsin for protein breakdown) -> Small Intestine (Bile emulsifies fats; Pancreatic trypsin/lipase complete digestion; Villi absorb nutrients into blood).
2. Respiration:
   Glucose (6C) breaks down into Pyruvate (3C) in cytoplasm (Glycolysis):
   - In presence of O₂ (Mitochondria): Pyruvate --> 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + 38 ATP (Aerobic).
   - In absence of O₂ (Yeast fermentation): Pyruvate --> 2 Ethanol + 2 CO₂ + 2 ATP.
   - In lack of O₂ (Human muscle cells during sprinting): Pyruvate --> 2 Lactic Acid + 2 ATP (causes muscle fatigue and cramps).
3. Transportation:
   - Double Circulation in Humans: Heart has 4 chambers. Deoxygenated blood from body enters Right Atrium -> Right Ventricle -> Lungs via Pulmonary Artery. Oxygenated blood from lungs enters Left Atrium via Pulmonary Veins -> Left Ventricle -> Aorta to whole body. Ensures complete separation of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood for high metabolic efficiency.
   - Plants: Xylem transports water/minerals unidirectionally via transpiration suction; Phloem translocates sucrose and amino acids bidirectionally using ATP energy.
4. Excretion:
   - Kidneys contain ~1 million filtration units called Nephrons.
   - Filtration Process: Glomerulus inside Bowman's Capsule performs ultrafiltration -> Renal Tubule selectively reabsorbs glucose, amino acids, salts, and major water -> Collecting duct collects concentrated Urine containing urea and uric acid.
formulas: Aerobic: C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ --> 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + 38 ATP
Anaerobic Yeast: C₆H₁₂O₆ --> 2 C₂H₅OH + 2 CO₂ + 2 ATP
Muscle Cramp: C₆H₁₂O₆ --> 2 Lactic Acid + 2 ATP
Blood Pressure: Normal Systolic/Diastolic = 120/80 mm Hg

ncertQuestions.question: What is the structural and functional unit of the human kidney? Explain its working.
ncertQuestions.answer: The Nephron is the structural and functional unit. Blood undergoes ultrafiltration under high pressure in the glomerulus inside Bowman's capsule. As the filtrate flows through the renal tubule, essential glucose, amino acids, and water are reabsorbed, leaving waste urea as urine.

summary: Life processes: Nutrition (villi absorption), Respiration (aerobic 38 ATP vs anaerobic lactic acid), Transportation (4-chambered double circulation heart, xylem/phloem), and Excretion via kidney nephrons.

subject: Biology
sectionTitle: Nervous System, Reflex Arc, Brain (Forebrain, Midbrain, Hindbrain), Plant Tropisms & Endocrine Glands
content:
Nervous System & Reflex Action:
- Neuron: Structural unit of nervous system. Electrical impulse travel: Dendrite -> Cell body (Cyton) -> Axon -> Synapse (chemical neurotransmitter gap).
- Reflex Arc: Involuntary, automatic, instantaneous response to a stimulus without conscious brain involvement:
  Receptor (skin) -> Sensory Neuron -> Spinal Cord (Relay Neuron) -> Motor Neuron -> Effector (Muscle contract).
Human Brain Anatomy:
1. Forebrain (Cerebrum): Largest part, seat of intelligence, memory, reasoning, voluntary movements, senses (hearing, sight, smell).
2. Midbrain: Controls involuntary visual and auditory reflex actions.
3. Hindbrain:
   - Cerebellum: Controls precision, posture, and body balance (walking in straight line, riding bicycle).
   - Medulla: Controls involuntary vital functions (blood pressure, salivation, vomiting).
   - Pons: Regulates respiration rhythm.
Coordination in Plants (Phytohormones):
- Plant Movements:
  1. Tropic Movements (Directional growth): Phototropism (towards light, mediated by Auxin), Geotropism (roots grow towards gravity), Hydrotropism (towards water), Chemotropism (pollen tube growth towards ovule).
  2. Nastic Movements (Non-directional turgor changes): Sensitive plant (Mimosa pudica 'Touch-me-not' leaves drop).
- Plant Hormones: Auxin (cell elongation), Gibberellins (stem growth), Cytokinins (cell division, fruit opening), Abscisic Acid (stress hormone, inhibits growth, wilting of leaves).
Animal Endocrine Hormones:
Pituitary (Growth hormone), Thyroid (Thyroxine, needs Iodine), Pancreas (Insulin), Adrenal (Adrenaline fight-or-flight), Testes (Testosterone), Ovaries (Estrogen).
formulas: Reflex Arc Pathway: Stimulus -> Receptor -> Sensory Neuron -> Spinal Cord -> Motor Neuron -> Effector

ncertQuestions.question: What is a reflex arc? Trace the sequence of events when you touch a hot object.
ncertQuestions.answer: A reflex arc is the nerve pathway of an automatic involuntary action. When touching a hot plate, heat receptors in skin fire sensory neurons to the spinal cord relay neuron, which instantly signals motor neurons to contract arm muscles and withdraw the hand.

summary: Nervous coordination operates via neurons and reflex arcs. Brain has cerebrum (memory), cerebellum (balance), and medulla (involuntary). Plant tropisms are driven by auxins; endocrine glands secrete hormones.

subject: Biology
sectionTitle: Asexual Reproduction (Fission, Regeneration, Spores), Flowering Plant Pollination & Human Reproductive Health
content:
Reproduction ensures the continuity of species.
I. Asexual Reproduction:
- Binary Fission: Amoeba, Leishmania. Multiple Fission: Plasmodium (malaria parasite).
- Budding: Hydra and Yeast.
- Fragmentation: Spirogyra.
- Regeneration: Planaria and Hydra can regenerate entire new organisms from cut fragments via specialized regenerative cells.
- Spore Formation: Rhizopus (bread mould) produces sporangia containing airborne spores.
- Vegetative Propagation: Layering, grafting, cutting; Bryophyllum leaf buds.
II. Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants (Angiosperms):
- Flower: Stamen (Male: Anther produces pollen grains) and Carpel/Pistil (Female: Stigma, Style, Ovary with ovules).
- Pollination: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma (Self vs Cross).
- Double Fertilisation: Pollen tube grows down style into ovule. One male gamete fuses with egg cell forming Zygote (Syngamy); second male gamete fuses with two polar nuclei forming Triploid Endosperm (Triple Fusion).
- Ovary becomes Fruit; Ovules become Seeds.
III. Human Reproduction:
- Male System: Testes produce sperms and testosterone (located in scrotum outside abdominal cavity to maintain 2-2.5°C lower temperature for spermatogenesis), vas deferens, prostate and seminal vesicles (provide fluid nutrition).
- Female System: Ovaries produce eggs and estrogen/progesterone, Fallopian tubes (site of fertilisation), Uterus (site of embryo implantation and placenta nourishment), Vagina.
- Menstruation: If egg is not fertilised, uterine lining sheds along with blood and mucus over 3 to 5 days every 28 days.
- Contraception: Barrier methods (condoms prevent STDs like HIV/Gonorrhoea), Chemical methods (oral pills), Surgical methods (Vasectomy in males, Tubectomy in females), Intrauterine devices (Copper-T).
formulas: Double Fertilisation: Syngamy (Egg + Sperm -> Zygote) + Triple Fusion (2 Polar Nuclei + Sperm -> Endosperm)
Scrotal Temperature = 2 to 2.5°C below core body temperature

ncertQuestions.question: What is the function of the placenta in human reproduction?
ncertQuestions.answer: The placenta is a disc-like vascular tissue embedded in the uterine wall containing villi. It provides a large surface area for glucose and oxygen to pass from mother's blood to the developing embryo, and removes waste products.

summary: Organisms reproduce asexually (fission, budding, regeneration) or sexually. Flowering plants undergo double fertilisation. Human fertilisation occurs in fallopian tubes, developing in uterus via placenta.

subject: Biology
sectionTitle: Mendel's Laws (Monohybrid & Dihybrid), Phenotype vs Genotype & Sex Determination in Humans
content:
Heredity is the biological transmission of traits from parents to offspring.
Gregor Johann Mendel's Experiments with Garden Pea (Pisum sativum):
1. Monohybrid Cross (One pair of contrasting traits, e.g., Tall TT × Dwarf tt):
   - F1 Generation: All plants are Tall (Tt, heterozygous).
   - F2 Generation (Selfing Tt × Tt):
     * Phenotypic Ratio = 3 Tall : 1 Dwarf (3:1).
     * Genotypic Ratio = 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt (1:2:1).
   - Law of Dominance: The allele that expresses in F1 is Dominant (T); the unexpressed allele is Recessive (t).
   - Law of Segregation: During gamete formation, the two alleles separate so each gamete carries only one allele.
2. Dihybrid Cross (Two pairs of traits, e.g., Round Yellow RRYY × Wrinkled Green rryy):
   - F1 Generation: All Round Yellow (RrYy).
   - F2 Generation:
     * Phenotypic Ratio = 9 Round Yellow : 3 Round Green : 3 Wrinkled Yellow : 1 Wrinkled Green (9:3:3:1).
   - Law of Independent Assortment: Alleles of different genes assort independently during gamete formation.
Sex Determination in Human Beings:
- Humans possess 23 pairs of chromosomes: 22 pairs are Autosomes and 1 pair are Sex Chromosomes.
- Human females have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes (XX).
- Human males have a mismatched pair (XY).
- All ova (eggs) produced by females carry an X chromosome. Sperms produced by males are 50% X-bearing and 50% Y-bearing.
  Egg (X) + Sperm (X) --> XX (Female child).
  Egg (X) + Sperm (Y) --> XY (Male child).
- Scientifically, the father's sperm strictly determines the biological sex of the child with 50% probability.
formulas: Mendel Monohybrid F2 Phenotypic Ratio: 3 : 1
Mendel Monohybrid F2 Genotypic Ratio: 1 (TT) : 2 (Tt) : 1 (tt)
Mendel Dihybrid F2 Phenotypic Ratio: 9 : 3 : 3 : 1
Sex Determination: Father's Sperm (X or Y) decides gender

ncertQuestions.question: How is the sex of a child determined in human beings?
ncertQuestions.answer: Human females produce eggs carrying only X chromosomes. Human males produce 50% X-bearing sperms and 50% Y-bearing sperms. If an X-sperm fertilises the egg, an XX female child is formed; if a Y-sperm fertilises the egg, an XY male child is formed. Hence, the father determines sex.

summary: Mendel established inheritance: monohybrid cross yields 3:1 phenotypic (1:2:1 genotypic) ratio; dihybrid cross yields 9:3:3:1. Paternal sex chromosomes (XY) determine human sex.

subject: Science
sectionTitle: Conventional vs Non-conventional Energy, Thermal, Hydro, Biogas, Solar, Nuclear & Environmental Consequences
content:
Classification of Energy Sources:
- Renewable Sources: Replaced naturally over short periods (Solar, Wind, Hydro, Biomass, Geothermal, Ocean).
- Non-renewable Sources: Exhaustible fossil fuels formed over millions of years (Coal, Petroleum, Natural Gas).
Conventional Sources of Energy:
1. Fossil Fuels: Cause greenhouse gas emissions, acid rain, air pollution.
2. Thermal Power Plants: Burning fossil fuels to produce steam driving turbine generators.
3. Hydro Power Plants: Converting gravitational potential energy of trapped river water in high dams into electrical energy (clean, renewable, but submerges forests and displaces communities).
4. Biomass & Biogas Plant:
   - Cow-dung, crop residue, and sewage decomposed by anaerobic microbes in a domed Biogas digester producing Biogas (75% Methane CH₄, burns with high calorific value without smoke) and organic manure rich in nitrogen and phosphorus.
Non-Conventional Sources of Energy:
1. Solar Energy: Solar cookers (black surface + glass sheet greenhouse trap + concave reflector), Solar cells made of Silicon converting sunlight directly into electricity (0.5-1 V per cell).
2. Wind Energy: Requires wind speeds > 15 km/h to spin windmill turbines.
3. Nuclear Energy:
   - Nuclear Fission: Heavy nucleus (Uranium-235) struck by neutron splits into lighter nuclei releasing massive energy: E = Δm · c² (Einstein). High risk of radioactive contamination and nuclear waste disposal.
   - Nuclear Fusion: Combining light nuclei (Hydrogen into Helium) at extreme temperature (powers Sun and stars).
formulas: Einstein Mass-Energy Equivalence: E = Δm · c²
Biogas Composition: ~75% Methane (CH₄) + CO₂ + H₂

ncertQuestions.question: What are the advantages of using biogas over burning dried cow-dung cakes?
ncertQuestions.answer: Biogas has high calorific value, burns cleanly without smoke or ash, does not cause respiratory pollution, and the spent slurry left behind serves as an excellent organic manure rich in nitrogen and phosphorus.

summary: Energy sources are renewable (solar, wind, biogas, hydro) or non-renewable (fossil fuels). Biogas produces 75% clean methane. Nuclear fission releases enormous energy via E = mc².

subject: Biology
sectionTitle: Ecosystem, Food Chains, Trophic Levels, 10% Law of Energy, Biological Magnification & Ozone Depletion
content:
An Ecosystem consists of Biotic components (producers, consumers, decomposers) and Abiotic factors (temperature, soil, rainfall, light).
Food Chains and Trophic Levels:
- A sequence of organisms where each feeds on the preceding one:
  Producer (Plants, 1st Trophic Level) -> Herbivore (Primary Consumer, 2nd Level) -> Carnivore (Secondary Consumer, 3rd Level) -> Top Carnivore (4th Level).
- 10% Law of Energy Transfer (Raymond Lindeman, 1942):
  Only 10% of the energy entering a trophic level is transferred to the next higher level as biomass; 90% is lost as heat, respiration, and metabolic activity:
  If Plants capture 10,000 J of solar energy: Herbivores get 1000 J -> Carnivores get 100 J -> Top carnivores get 10 J.
  Because energy diminishes rapidly, food chains rarely exceed 4 to 5 trophic levels.
Biological Magnification:
- The progressive accumulation of non-biodegradable harmful toxic chemicals (like DDT pesticide) in body tissues at progressively higher trophic levels.
- Top consumers (Humans) accumulate the highest toxic concentration because chemicals cannot be excreted or metabolized.
Environmental Issues:
1. Ozone Layer Depletion: Stratospheric Ozone (O₃) shields Earth from lethal UV radiation. Synthetic Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) release chlorine radicals that destroy ozone (UNEP 1987 Montreal Protocol froze CFC production).
2. Solid Waste Management: Differentiating Biodegradable (organic food) from Non-biodegradable (plastics) waste.
formulas: Lindeman's 10% Law: E_(n+1) = 0.10 × E_n
Ozone Formation: O₂ + UV -> O + O; O + O₂ -> O₃
Biomagnification: Toxicant concentration increases up trophic levels

ncertQuestions.question: What is biological magnification? Will the levels of this magnification be different at different levels of the ecosystem?
ncertQuestions.answer: Biological magnification is the progressive increase in the concentration of non-biodegradable toxic substances (e.g. pesticides) at each successive trophic level in a food chain. It is highest in top carnivores (such as humans) at the peak of the pyramid.

summary: Ecosystem food chains obey Lindeman's 10% energy law (90% lost at each level). Non-biodegradable toxicants concentrate at top trophic levels via biological magnification. Stratospheric ozone shields UV.

subject: Mathematics
sectionTitle: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, HCF & LCM Relationship, Proof of Irrationality of √2, √3
content:
Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic:
Every composite number can be expressed (factorised) as a product of primes, and this prime factorisation is unique, apart from the order in which the prime factors occur.
HCF and LCM of Two Positive Integers a and b:
- HCF (Highest Common Factor): Product of the smallest power of each common prime factor involved in the numbers.
- LCM (Lowest Common Multiple): Product of the greatest power of each prime factor involved in the numbers.
- Important Fundamental Relation:
  HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
  => LCM(a, b) = (a × b) / HCF(a, b).
Proof of Irrationality (Proof by Contradiction):
- Theorem: If p is a prime number and p divides a², then p divides a (where a is a positive integer).
- To prove √2 is irrational:
  Assume √2 is rational = a/b (where a and b are co-prime integers, b ≠ 0).
  2 = a² / b² => a² = 2b² (so 2 divides a², hence 2 divides a => a = 2c).
  (2c)² = 2b² => 4c² = 2b² => b² = 2c² (so 2 divides b).
  Thus, 2 is a common factor of both a and b, which contradicts that a and b are co-prime.
  Therefore, √2 is irrational.
- Decimal Expansions: A rational number p/q has a terminating decimal expansion if and only if the prime factorisation of q is of the form 2^n · 5^m (where n, m are non-negative integers).
formulas: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b
Terminating Decimal condition: Denominator q = 2ⁿ · 5ᵐ
Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: Unique Prime Factorisation
summary: Every composite number has a unique prime factorisation. HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) = a × b. Numbers like √2 and √3 are proved irrational by contradiction. Fractions terminate if denominator q = 2ⁿ·5ᵐ.

subject: Mathematics
chapterTitle: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
sectionTitle: Graphical Method, Consistency Conditions, Substitution & Elimination Methods
content:
General Form of a Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables:
a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0
a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0
Consistency Conditions (Ratios of Coefficients):
1. Intersecting Lines (Unique Solution):
   a₁ / a₂ ≠ b₁ / b₂  => System is Consistent with exactly 1 unique solution.
2. Coincident Lines (Infinitely Many Solutions):
   a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ = c₁ / c₂  => System is Consistent and Dependent with infinitely many solutions.
3. Parallel Lines (No Solution):
   a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ ≠ c₁ / c₂  => System is Inconsistent with 0 solutions.
Algebraic Solution Methods:
- Substitution Method: Express one variable in terms of the other from one equation and substitute into the second equation.
- Elimination Method: Multiply equations by non-zero constants to make coefficients of one variable numerically equal, then add or subtract equations to eliminate that variable.
formulas: Unique Solution: a₁ / a₂ ≠ b₁ / b₂
Infinitely Many Solutions: a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ = c₁ / c₂
No Solution (Parallel): a₁ / a₂ = b₁ / b₂ ≠ c₁ / c₂

ncertQuestions.question: Check whether the pair of equations 2x + 3y = 8 and 4x + 6y = 7 is consistent or inconsistent.
ncertQuestions.answer: a1/a2 = 2/4 = 1/2. b1/b2 = 3/6 = 1/2. c1/c2 = -8/-7 = 8/7. Since a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2, the lines are parallel and have no solution. The system is inconsistent.

summary: Linear systems a1x+b1y+c1=0 and a2x+b2y+c2=0: unique solution if a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2; infinite if a1/a2=b1/b2=c1/c2; no solution if a1/a2=b1/b2≠c1/c2. Solved via substitution or elimination.

subject: Mathematics
sectionTitle: General Term (a_n), Common Difference (d) & Sum of First n Terms (S_n)
content:
An Arithmetic Progression (AP) is a sequence of numbers in which each term is obtained by adding a fixed number d (Common Difference) to the preceding term, except the first term a:
AP: a, a + d, a + 2d, a + 3d, ...
- Common Difference d = a_(k+1) - a_k (can be positive, negative, or zero).
nth Term of an AP (General Term):
a_n = a + (n - 1) · d
Where: a = first term, d = common difference, n = term number.
- If an AP has m terms, the last term l = a_m = a + (m - 1)d.
Sum of First n Terms of an AP (S_n):
S_n = n / 2 · [2a + (n - 1) · d]
Or, when first term a and last term l are known:
S_n = n / 2 · (a + l)
- Sum of first n positive integers: S_n = n(n + 1) / 2.
- nth term from sum: a_n = S_n - S_(n-1).
formulas: nth Term: a_n = a + (n - 1) · d
Sum of n terms: S_n = n / 2 · [2a + (n - 1) · d]
Sum with last term: S_n = n / 2 · (a + l)
Sum of first n natural numbers: S_n = n(n + 1) / 2

ncertQuestions.question: Find the 20th term and the sum of first 20 terms of the AP: 2, 7, 12, ...

summary: In an AP, each term differs by d. The nth term is a_n = a + (n-1)d. The sum of n terms is S_n = (n/2)[2a + (n-1)d] = (n/2)(a + l). Sum of first n integers is n(n+1)/2.

subject: Mathematics
sectionTitle: Distance Formula, Section Formula (Internal Division) & Midpoint Formula
content:
Coordinate plane with x-axis (Abscissa) and y-axis (Ordinate) intersecting at origin (0, 0).
1. Distance Formula:
The Euclidean distance d between two points P(x₁, y₁) and Q(x₂, y₂):
d = √[(x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²]
- Distance of a point P(x, y) from origin (0, 0): d = √(x² + y²).
2. Section Formula (Internal Division):
The coordinates of point P(x, y) which divides the line segment joining A(x₁, y₁) and B(x₂, y₂) internally in the ratio m₁ : m₂ are:
x = (m₁ · x₂ + m₂ · x₁) / (m₁ + m₂)
y = (m₁ · y₂ + m₂ · y₁) / (m₁ + m₂)
3. Midpoint Formula:
When P is the exact midpoint dividing AB in 1 : 1 ratio:
x = (x₁ + x₂) / 2
y = (y₁ + y₂) / 2
- Centroid of a Triangle with vertices (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), (x₃, y₃):
  G = ((x₁ + x₂ + x₃) / 3, (y₁ + y₂ + y₃) / 3).
formulas: Distance Formula: d = √[(x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²]
Distance from Origin: d = √(x² + y²)
Section Formula: x = (m₁x₂ + m₂x₁) / (m₁ + m₂), y = (m₁y₂ + m₂y₁) / (m₁ + m₂)
Midpoint Formula: x = (x₁ + x₂)/2, y = (y₁ + y₂)/2

ncertQuestions.question: Find the coordinates of the point which divides the join of (-1, 7) and (4, -3) in the ratio 2 : 3.

summary: Distance between (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is √[(x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²]. Section formula divides segments in ratio m1:m2: [(m1x2+m2x1)/(m1+m2), (m1y2+m2y1)/(m1+m2)]. Midpoint is [(x1+x2)/2, (y1+y2)/2].

subject: Mathematics
sectionTitle: Mean of Grouped Data (Direct & Assumed Mean), Mode of Grouped Data & Median
content:
Measures of Central Tendency for Grouped Data:
1. Mean (x̄):
   - Direct Method: x̄ = Σ(f_i · x_i) / Σf_i  (where x_i is class mark = (Upper limit + Lower limit) / 2).
   - Assumed Mean Method: x̄ = a + [Σ(f_i · d_i) / Σf_i]  (where d_i = x_i - a, and a is assumed mean).
2. Mode:
   The value among the observations having maximum frequency:
   Mode = l + [(f₁ - f₀) / (2f₁ - f₀ - f₂)] · h
   Where:
   l = lower limit of modal class (class with highest frequency f₁)
   h = size of class interval
   f₁ = frequency of modal class
   f₀ = frequency of class preceding modal class
   f₂ = frequency of class succeeding modal class.
3. Median:
   The middle value of distribution dividing it into two equal halves:
   Median = l + [((n/2) - cf) / f] · h
   Where:
   l = lower limit of median class (class where cumulative frequency cf reaches n/2)
   n = total number of observations (Σf_i)
   cf = cumulative frequency of class preceding median class
   f = frequency of median class
   h = class size.
Empirical Relationship:
3 · Median = Mode + 2 · Mean.
formulas: Direct Mean: x̄ = Σ(f_i · x_i) / Σf_i
Assumed Mean: x̄ = a + [Σ(f_i · d_i) / Σf_i]
Mode = l + [(f₁ - f₀) / (2f₁ - f₀ - f₂)] · h
Median = l + [((n/2) - cf) / f] · h
Empirical Relation: 3 · Median = Mode + 2 · Mean

ncertQuestions.question: What is the empirical relationship between the three measures of central tendency?
ncertQuestions.answer: 3 × Median = Mode + 2 × Mean (or Mode = 3 Median - 2 Mean).

summary: Mean is calculated via direct Σfixi/Σfi or assumed mean a + Σfidi/Σfi. Mode = l + [(f1-f0)/(2f1-f0-f2)]h. Median = l + [((n/2)-cf)/f]h. Linked by 3·Median = Mode + 2·Mean.
